bugs.description: Uses > 90, so a score of exactly 90 gets a B instead of an A
An empty class divides by zero and returns NaN
Array.prototype.sort reorders the caller's scores array in place
Uses > 60, so a score of exactly 60 counts as a fail even though 60 is a pass
sort() without a compare function sorts numbers as text (100 before 65); the median is also wrong for an even number of scores
